questions.stem: Naresh is preparing a talk on satyagraha for his school assembly and wants to explain to the audience why people who were oppressing others had to be won over rather than beaten down. Consider the following statements. 1. Satyagraha required that people, including the oppressors, be persuaded to see the truth instead of being forced to accept truth through the use of violence. 2. This is how a struggle could succeed, because satyagraha is not physical force and the satyagrahi does not inflict pain on the adversary or seek his destruction, so that truth was bound to ultimately triumph. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.stem: Rehan is reading about the year 1918 and asks why a satyagraha was then organised to support the peasants of the Kheda district of Gujarat. Consider the following statements. 1. The peasants of Kheda could not pay the revenue because of crop failure and a plague epidemic, and they were demanding that revenue collection be relaxed. 2. The Kheda satyagraha was a response to the Rowlatt Act of 1919, which gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.stem: Farida is asked to narrate what happened in the enclosed ground of Jallianwalla Bagh on 13 April 1919, when a large crowd had gathered there. Consider the following statements. 1. General Dyer blocked the exit points and opened fire on the crowd only after the crowd had begun to attack banks, post offices and railway stations. 2. Everyone in that crowd had come only to attend the annual Baisakhi fair and nobody had come to protest. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are false.
